div.p: XSLT stylesheets can be debugged with SaxonJ in VS Code's debugger: set breakpoints, step through templates, functions and multi-line XPath expressions, and inspect variables, the context item and the output written so far.
If you're new to debugging in VS Code, see Debugging in the VS Code documentation for the debug toolbar, views and keyboard shortcuts.
For debugging by adding xsl:message instructions to the stylesheet, see Debugging with xsl:message.
div.aside: Requirements: SaxonJ 12 or later - any edition, including Saxon-HE - set with the XSLT.tasks.saxonJar setting, and a Java runtime on the PATH. Debugging with SaxonJS or SaxonC isn't supported. For XPath 4.0 syntax in an XSLT 4.0 stylesheet, Saxon-PE or Saxon-EE is needed.
div.p: Open the stylesheet and set a breakpoint - click in the margin to the left of a line number, or press F9. Then start debugging in any of these ways:

ul.li: the Debug Stylesheet with SaxonJ button in the editor title bar
XSLT: Debug Stylesheet with SaxonJ from the Command Palette
F5, when there's no launch.json - or the Debug Stylesheet link in the Run and Debug view

div.p: The stylesheet runs as Quick Run runs it: with the XML context file, or from xsl:initial-template when there's no context file. It uses the same Quick Run task, so parameters added to that task also apply when debugging. When the stylesheet is imported or included by another, you're offered the choice of running the parent stylesheet instead.

p.i: The Run and Debug View provides options for how to launch the debugger.

div.p: With no launch.json, the Run and Debug view offers Debug Active Stylesheet, and a Debug task label configuration for each xslt task in tasks.json (see XSLT: Tasks). create a launch.json file adds these to a new launch.json.
A launch configuration uses the xslt-saxon debugger type, with one of:

ul.li: "quickRun": true - the stylesheet in the active editor, as Quick Run runs it
"task" - the label of an xslt task in tasks.json, whose properties are used; properties set in the configuration override them
the same properties as an xslt task, such as xsltFile, xmlSource, initialTemplate, resultPath and parameters

div.p: "stopOnEntry": true pauses at the first instruction executed. In launch.json, Add Configuration... offers four snippets: XSLT (Saxon): Debug Active Stylesheet, Debug a Task, Debug Stylesheet (with a source file) and Debug from Initial Template. See Debug configuration in the VS Code documentation for more on launch.json.
A breakpoint can be set on a line where an XSLT instruction or a literal result element starts. A breakpoint anywhere in a multi-line start tag is moved to the tag's first line.
Breakpoints can also be set inside a multi-line XPath expression - see Stepping through XPath.
div.h5: Conditional breakpoints, hit counts and logpoints
div.p: Right-click in the margin and choose Add Conditional Breakpoint... or Add Logpoint... - or right-click an existing breakpoint and choose Edit Breakpoint:

ul.li: Expression - an XPath expression, evaluated where the breakpoint is, with its variables and context item, e.g. @customer = 'Grace' or $total gt 30. If the expression raises an error, execution pauses and the error is shown.
Hit Count - 5 (the 5th hit), >5, >=5, <5, <=5 or %5 (every 5th hit). With an expression too, only the hits where the expression is true are counted.
Log Message - a logpoint writes the message to the Debug Console without pausing. Each {xpath} in the message is replaced by its value, e.g. {$line/@product} costs {f:line-total($line)}.

p.i: Setting a conditional breakpoint with an XPath expression.

div.p: To stop whenever a stylesheet function or named template is called, without finding where it's declared, click + (Add Function Breakpoint) in the Breakpoints view and enter its name. The function or template can be in any module of the stylesheet, including imported and included modules. Execution stops at the start of the function or template, where the Variables view shows its parameters - for a named template, these are the values passed to it.

ul.li: The name is written as it is where the function or template is declared, with the same prefix, e.g. f:total or cell - or as an EQName, e.g. Q{urn:f}total. A () after the name is allowed.
An arity selects one version of a function, e.g. f:total#2. With no arity, every version of the function stops.
Conditions and hit counts work as for line breakpoints - right-click the breakpoint and choose Edit Condition or Edit Hit Count. The condition can use the parameters, e.g. $n = 2.

div.p: A name that isn't valid is shown as unverified straight away. A function or template that isn't in the stylesheet - or a function with no version of the arity given - is shown as unverified once the stylesheet has compiled; hover over the breakpoint for the reason. Template rules - templates with a match attribute - aren't stopped at this way, even when they also have a name: use a line breakpoint instead.
The Breakpoints view has two options for errors:

ul.li: Dynamic Errors (on by default) - pauses where a dynamic error that ends the transform is raised, including xsl:message with terminate="yes". The error's code and message are shown, and the variables at that point can be inspected.
Errors Caught by xsl:try (off by default) - also pauses at errors that an xsl:try catches. This needs Saxon 12.5 or later.

p.i: The debugger paused on a dynamic error.

div.p: A static error - one Saxon finds when it compiles the stylesheet - can't be paused at, as the stylesheet never runs. This includes a type error that Saxon can tell will always happen: for example, an xsl:variable with as="xs:string" whose select is count(...), which is always an xs:integer. The session then ends with a notification that gives the first error and its line, and the errors are listed in the Problems view.
The debug toolbar has the usual Continue (F5), Step Over (F10), Step Into (F11), Step Out (⇧F11), Pause and Stop commands. In XSLT terms:

ul.li: Step Over goes to the next line in the current template or function, without stopping in the templates and functions it calls - for example, with xsl:apply-templates or xsl:call-template.
Step Into stops in each template rule, named template or function called, and in a global variable when it's evaluated.
Step Out continues until the current template or function returns.
The bodies of xsl:for-each, xsl:for-each-group and xsl:iterate are stepped through, not over, for each item.

div.p: Stepping goes line by line: execution stops once each time it reaches a line, not once for each instruction on it. A breakpoint in a loop stops once for each iteration.

A multi-line XPath expression in a select, test or value attribute can be stepped through: use Step Into at the instruction, or set a breakpoint on a line of the expression. Execution stops on each line where a part of the expression starts.

The expression is evaluated separately, in the instruction's context, so that each part reports its own line. It appears in the call stack as, for example, xsl:variable/@select (XPath), and its result is shown in the Debug Console, e.g. ▸ $line-totals (xsl:variable/@select, lines 25-28) returned (6.75, 10.8, 15.75). The instruction itself then runs as usual. The body of an inline function is stepped through each time it's called - for example, by fold-left().

p.i: Evaluation context and call stack in the Run and Debug view when execution is paused.

div.p: The Call Stack view has a frame for each:

ul.li: template rule, with its match pattern and mode, e.g. xsl:template match="order" mode="summary"
named template, e.g. xsl:template name="header"
function, by name and arity, e.g. f:line-total#1
global variable or parameter being evaluated, e.g. xsl:variable $orders
xsl:for-each, xsl:for-each-group or xsl:iterate instruction, with its select expression
XPath expression being stepped through, e.g. xsl:variable/@select (XPath)

div.p: Selecting a frame shows its location in the editor, and its variables in the Variables view.
The Variables view has four sections:

ul.li: Locals - the parameters of the template, function or xsl:iterate, then the variables in scope - from xsl:variable, and from XPath for, let, some and every expressions, including a positional at $pos variable. Tunnel parameters are shown as $name (tunnel).
Context - the context item (.), position() and last(), and where they apply, current-group(), current-grouping-key() and each regex-group().
Globals - the global variables and parameters, sorted by name. A global variable that hasn't been used yet is evaluated when it's shown.
Output - which result is being written to, or that a temporary tree is being built (for example, an xsl:variable's content), and the end of each output written so far.

div.p: Nodes, maps, arrays and sequences can be expanded. An element shows its attributes, then its child nodes, with the line number of the element in its source document. Long values are truncated, and an expanded value shows at most 1000 items.

While paused, the value of each variable declared earlier in the current template or function is shown at the end of the line where it's declared. This applies to xsl:variable and xsl:param, and in XPath, to let, for, some and every variables and inline function parameters. The VS Code setting debug.inlineValues turns this off.
div.h3: Watch, hover and the Debug Console
div.p: While paused, type an XPath expression at the prompt at the bottom of the Debug Console and press Enter to evaluate it - for example, line[@qty gt 1]/@product on an order element, or count(current-group()) in xsl:for-each-group. Expressions added to the Watch view are evaluated in the same way, and again each time execution pauses.
Expressions are evaluated in the context of the call stack frame selected in the Call Stack view, with:

ul.li: the variables in scope, and the context item
the stylesheet's namespace declarations and functions, e.g. f:line-total($line)
current(), current-group(), current-grouping-key() and regex-group(), which give their values where execution is paused

div.p: Results are shown, and can be expanded, as in the Variables view. Hovering over a variable reference such as $total, or the name in a variable declaration, shows its value.

The output written so far - the principal result, and each xsl:result-document - opens beside the stylesheet at the first pause where there is some, and is updated at each pause. It's serialized by Saxon as the result is, but indented for readability, and shown in the language of its output method: XML, HTML, JSON or plain text. The result itself is written as the stylesheet specifies.

ul.li: XSLT: Show Debug Output, or its button on the debug toolbar, opens the output at any time. When there's more than one output, you choose which to show.
The XSLT.debug.openOutput setting turns off opening the output automatically.
xsl:message output, and the result when there's no resultPath, are written to the Debug Console.

div.p: When the session ends, a notification offers to Open the result file - or, for HTML, to Open in Browser.

Saxon's error messages in the Debug Console are linked to the location of the error. The errors are also listed in the Problems view, as for XSLT tasks. A file's errors are removed from the Problems view when the file is edited, as they may no longer apply.

The debugger-demo sample has a stylesheet, debug-xpath.xsl, and an XML file, orders.xml. Open orders.xml, so it becomes the XML context file, then debug-xpath.xsl, and start debugging. Things to try are listed in a comment at the top of the stylesheet, including:

ul.li: stepping through a multi-line for ... return expression, and into a function it calls
a breakpoint inside an expression in xsl:for-each-group, with count(current-group()) in the Watch view
conditional breakpoints, hit counts and a logpoint
pausing at a dynamic error, after changing a price in orders.xml to n/a

For debugging, the stylesheet is compiled without optimization, so all variables can be inspected. Saxon still evaluates constant expressions when it compiles - e.g. an xsl:if whose test uses only constant values - and an instruction removed that way can't be stopped at.
Values can't be changed in the Variables view.
Only modules loaded from files can be stopped in.

div.p: When a debug session doesn't start, a notification gives the reason, with a Show Output button - for example, when Java isn't on the PATH, the Saxon jar doesn't exist, or the Java runtime is too old for the Saxon jar.
The XSLT Debugger log, in the Output panel, shows how each session was launched: the Java command line, the Saxon product, the Java runtime and the Saxon options used.
